response.passage: Rohan is helping his grandfather build a water storage tank in their garden. The tank is a large cylinder with a radius of 1 meter and a height of 2 meters. Rohan calculates the space inside the tank to determine how much water it can hold. He remembers that volume is measured in cubic units, so he calculates the volume as 2π cubic meters. His grandfather then asks him to paint the outside of the tank. Rohan knows that the total surface area of a cylinder includes the curved surface area plus the areas of both the top and bottom circular bases, calculated as 2πr(h + r). He carefully measures the surface area to buy enough paint. Later, they decide to melt down a solid metal sphere with a radius of 3 cm to make smaller spheres, each with a radius of 1 cm. Rohan realizes that the number of small spheres is not just the ratio of the radii, but the ratio of their volumes, which is 27. Finally, they check a small container that holds 1000 cubic centimeters of water. Rohan correctly notes that this volume is exactly equivalent to 1 litre, ensuring they have the right capacity for their garden project.
response.summary: Rohan calculates the volume and surface area of a cylindrical tank for his garden project. He also learns about the relationship between sphere volumes and liquid capacity units.
